## Scope and evidence

This second mapping notebook compares the user's supplied description of the
legacy cleaned database with the saved pipeline products inspected on
2026-11-04. The requested interface consists of clinic spatial metadata,
clinic-month reporting metadata, healthshed polygons, a bilingual diagnosis
dictionary, and manageable diagnosis partitions.

The pipeline already produces most of these components. A compatible release
still needs a diagnosis-ID reconciliation, a decision about ambiguous monthly
database codes, and a versioned export procedure. The recommendations below
are proposals; **no decision in the guidance table has been approved or
implemented by this review**.

The inspection read completed Parquet products and existing targets. It did
not rebuild the pipeline, modify source data, compare all historical diagnosis
values, or establish full scientific equivalence with a legacy release.
Counts describe this saved state, not permanent acceptance thresholds.

This notebook contains aggregate observations from governed data. It is kept
outside the book's chapter list, consistent with the
[data-governance guidance](../../03_misc-data-governance.qmd), pending review
for inclusion in a rendered Manual.

## Findings that need resolution

### Diagnosis identity changes despite matching file structure

The supplied description says `V1` through `V3621`. The current dictionary
and both inspected reference dictionaries instead have 3,595 rows. This
does not establish that 26 variables were lost; the description may refer
to a different version. Identify the authoritative baseline before changing
the dictionary's size.

There is a separate, demonstrated ID compatibility issue. Among 2,096
French descriptions that occur exactly once in each of the current and
archived dictionaries, all match by text, but **1,954 have different `V`
identifiers**. For example, `Accouchement 10 - 14 ans` is archived as `V237`
and currently appears as `V236`. These exact description matches diagnose
label movement; they do not prove that all underlying wave expressions agree.

[Page 21](../21_page-construct-diagnosis-dictionary.qmd) assigns `V` IDs by
row position and partitions variables by position. Consequently, reproducing
the same column names and number of files does not establish stable diagnosis
identity. Build a reviewed crosswalk using definitions and wave expressions,
resolving `X` terms through each version's own source schema. Preserve legacy
IDs and file assignments for equivalent definitions; explicitly version any
definition changes. Do not match or renumber variables from descriptions alone.

The missing English description is `V2531`, whose current French description
is `T10 II: Femmes enceintes PCPER CDI`. Its wording requires a reviewed
translation rather than an inferred expansion of an unfamiliar acronym.

### Historical code ambiguity expands reporting rows

Each of the 33 repeated reporting keys has two distinct historical database
codes and one retained `fname`. All 66 affected rows obtain their codes from
the historical crosswalk. The [page 25 join](../25_page-combine-clinic-metadata.qmd)
preserves these multiple code matches. They are not exact duplicate rows,
so `distinct()` cannot resolve the ambiguity.

The diagnosis files remain uniquely keyed. The decision concerns how a scalar
`clinic_database_code` should represent multiple historical codes, not whether
to remove or combine diagnosis observations. With the current population and
calendar, the resolved metadata would have 768,960 rows: 550,932 reported and
218,028 nonreporting clinic-months.

### Export format and data semantics need an explicit contract

The current pipeline stores tabular handoffs in Parquet; healthshed geometry
remains an ordinary spatial target. The supplied R example instead expects
CSV dictionaries and Feather diagnosis files. Keeping Parquet preserves table
shape but requires changing the reader. Supporting the existing example
unchanged requires a compatibility export and a reviewed exception to the
[Parquet artifact convention](../../02_misc-project-contract.qmd).

The actual legacy diagnosis writer uses `cAnnee` and `cPeriode`, matching our
current files. Its reporting metadata uses `year` and `month`. The supplied
prose's English date terms are not evidence that diagnosis columns should be
renamed. Similarly, the actual dictionary field is `wave1_colname`, not the
prose's `wave1_colname1`.

Retain distinctions between entered zero, missing values, and `-1`. The
implementation also reserves `-99` for unresolved duplicate reductions;
the inspected reduction audits have no error decisions. Document the
different earlier-wave and W3 aggregation rules rather than applying a
blanket zero replacement during export. Reporting eligibility is established
before projecting an individual diagnosis partition, so an all-missing
partition row does not necessarily mean the clinic failed to report.

Facility type and public/private status are cross-sectional attributes with
recorded source precedence and inference rules. They are not validated
monthly histories. The 2022 healthsheds likewise remain a fixed geographic
reference for diagnoses extending through 2024. Preserve category-overlap
and wave-transition cautions, and recalculate dated coverage statements such
as the historical count of 16 clinics lacking healthsheds.

## Implementation handoff after decisions

1. Record D1–D3 and resolve diagnosis identity and historical code ambiguity
   in their owning transformations or an explicitly reviewed compatibility
   mapping. Keep scientific decisions out of ad hoc serialization code.
2. Implement the selected interface through
   [release packaging](../../releases/19_page-package-release.qmd), consuming
   curated products without reimplementing cleaning. Move rejected
   `*_wrong_fname` partitions to a distinct user-facing directory if included;
   keep optional reference/audit products separate from primary diagnosis files.
3. Verify unique clinic and clinic-month keys; identical diagnosis partition
   key sets; exact dictionary-column correspondence; reporting/source
   agreement; metadata reporting totals; spatial joins and empty geometry
   handling; and export round-trip equality, including sentinel values.
4. Run the user's pneumonia-loading workflow against the selected package
   format. Record the exact artifacts, accepted definition differences,
   dependency versions, and checksums through
   [release verification](../../releases/21_page-verify-release.qmd).

Full historical value parity and accepted clinical definition differences
remain separate evidence requirements. Passing file-shape checks alone is
insufficient to claim that the new release reproduces legacy analyses.
